alert.summary: EDR flagged repeated outbound connections from powershell.exe on WKS-042 to a single external destination.

findings.finding: At 2026-08-24T10:42:11Z powershell.exe (PID 8124) executed on WKS-042 with command line 'powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Users\svc_backup\AppData\Roaming\win_update.ps1' — hidden, execution-policy-bypassed launch of a user-profile script.

The script decoded an embedded base64 blob, passed it to Invoke-Expression, and started 'Start-SyncLoop' targeting metrics-telemetry-cdn.example:443 every 15 seconds — consistent with the EDR beaconing detection.
All activity associated with the malicious chain (cmd, powershell, file creation, registry persistence) ran under service account CORP\svc_backup.

Process ancestry is services.exe (SYSTEM) -> explorer.exe (CORP\jmalik, started 10:41:58Z) -> cmd.exe '/c winlogon-update.bat' (CORP\svc_backup, 10:42:09Z) -> powershell.exe (CORP\svc_backup, 10:42:11Z); the process tree explicitly flags proc_0049 (cmd) and proc_0051 (powershell) as suspicious.

Anomalous user-context switch exists in the lineage: interactive shell explorer.exe running as CORP\jmalik directly spawned cmd.exe as CORP\svc_backup, suggesting possible credential theft or token manipulation of svc_backup.

File artifact C:\Users\svc_backup\AppData\Roaming\win_update.ps1 was created 2026-08-24T10:42:20Z, size 1489 bytes, SHA256 b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184e0f3a1d2f4a5b6c7d8e9f00112233445, UNSIGNED (no signer), quarantine status none, and is tied to executing PID 8124.
Persistence was established via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value 'WinUpdateSync' set at 10:42:22Z to relaunch the same powershell command at logon.

The EDR alert (rule POWERSHELL_OUTBOUND_BEACON, severity HIGH) fired at 2026-08-24T10:43:01Z after observing 12 outbound connections in 180s from PID 8124 to a single external endpoint; full kill-chain timeline spans 10:41:58Z–10:43:01Z (~63s).

The suspicious PowerShell process (PID 8124) on WKS-042 resolved 'metrics-telemetry-cdn.example' (A record, TTL 300) to external IP 203.0.113.66 via internal resolver 10.20.0.53, querying it twice within 32 seconds immediately before the beaconing activity.

powershell.exe (PID 8124) made four short-lived outbound TCP sessions from 10.20.31.42 to a single concentrated external destination 203.0.113.66:443 between 10:42:17Z and 10:43:02Z, matching the EDR POWERSHELL_OUTBOUND_BEACON detection.

MEASURED: The four outbound flows occur at exact 15-second intervals (10:42:17→10:42:32→10:42:47→10:43:02, three intervals of precisely 15s, 0s observed jitter), with highly consistent transfer sizes of 798-812 bytes sent and 198-210 bytes received per session and uniform 2-second durations.

INTERPRETATION: The combination of machine-precision 15s callbacks, near-identical small payloads (~800B up/~200B down), fixed 2s session length, single-destination concentration, and origin from powershell.exe is characteristic of automated HTTPS C2 beaconing rather than human browsing.

Threat intelligence confirms both primary indicators as C2 infrastructure: domain 'metrics-telemetry-cdn.example' is rated MALICIOUS/c2 (confidence 0.93, first seen 2026-08-20) and its resolving IP 203.0.113.66 is rated SUSPICIOUS/c2-infrastructure (confidence 0.88, first seen 2026-08-21).

The same PowerShell PID 8124 also queried 'update-sync-check.example' (A → 198.51.100.23, low TTL 60s) at 10:43:00Z one second before the final beacon, but no network flow to 198.51.100.23 was ever observed — consistent with an attempted-but-unconnected fallback/backup C2 endpoint, though this link remains unconfirmed.

Other traffic on WKS-042 appears benign business activity unrelated to the alert: browser (msedge.exe, PID 3120) and outlook.exe connected only to internal corporate servers (portal.corp.example→10.20.5.10, mail.corp.example→10.20.5.22), and the externally-resolved 'fonts.gstatic-cdn.example' (198.51.100.90) had no threat-feed record and no associated powershell activity.

The PowerShell script decodes a base64-encoded payload at runtime; the decoded body is the placeholder string 'SYNTHETIC-DEMO-PAYLOAD', so full payload logic is NOT observable — PROVEN: runtime base64 decoding occurs; LIKELY: it is a staged dropper/beacon component whose final stage is fetched or executed post-decode.

The script references two external network destinations — domain 'metrics-telemetry-cdn.example' and IP '203.0.113.66' — and performs outbound HTTP requests consistent with the EDR POWERSHELL_OUTBOUND_BEACON detection.

The on-host artifact is 'C:\Users\svc_backup\AppData\Roaming\win_update.ps1' (WKS-042), 1,489 bytes, UNSIGNED with no signer, created/modified 2026-08-24T10:42:20Z — ~41 seconds before the 10:43:01Z EDR alert — executed by PID 8124, referenced by a persistence event (evt_0196), and NOT quarantined.

Obfuscation/evasion techniques present: runtime base64 payload decode (obfuscation.base64), an infinite sleep loop typical of C2 beaconing (persistence.sleep_loop), and blanket error suppression to evade logging (discovery.error_suppress).

Threat intel confirms the deployed script's SHA-256 (b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184e0f3a1d2f4a5b6c7d8e9f00112233445) is MALICIOUS, categorized as a dropper with 0.90 feed confidence (first seen 2026-08-24T10:42:20Z, matching its creation time).

Threat intel independently rates the referenced C2 domain 'metrics-telemetry-cdn.example' MALICIOUS/c2 (confidence 0.93, first seen 2026-08-20) and the IP '203.0.113.66' SUSPICIOUS/c2-infrastructure (confidence 0.88, first seen 2026-08-21), corroborating the beacon destination attribution from static analysis.

final_report.executive_summary: EDR alert INC-2026-0042 on WKS-042 is CONFIRMED malicious: an unsigned, base64-obfuscated PowerShell dropper (win_update.ps1, SHA256 b1946ac9...3445 — feed-rated MALICIOUS) executed under CORP\svc_backup with hidden window and ExecutionPolicy Bypass, established HKCU Run-key persistence ('WinUpdateSync'), and beacons to attacker infrastructure metrics-telemetry-cdn.example / 203.0.113.66:443 on a machine-precision 15-second cycle corroborated by DNS logs, netflows, and threat intel. Correlated risk scored 100/100 (CRITICAL, avg confidence 0.905); with human approval the host was isolated at 09:55:47Z, cutting the C2 channel while remediation proceeds.
final_report.conclusion:
VERDICT: TRUE POSITIVE — active PowerShell HTTPS C2 beaconing from WKS-042, contained by endpoint isolation at 2026-08-26T09:55:47Z with human approval.

STRONGEST EVIDENCE CHAIN: The EDR detection rule POWERSHELL_OUTBOUND_BEACON fired at 10:43:01Z after 12 outbound connections in 180s from a single powershell.exe PID [windows_events:evt_0197] -> that process was launched at 10:42:11Z hidden with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass running C:\Users\svc_backup\AppData\Roaming\win_update.ps1 under CORP\svc_backup [windows_events:evt_0192, process_tree:proc_0051] -> the payload is an UNSIGNED 1,489-byte script whose SHA256 b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184e0f3a1d2f4a5b6c7d8e9f00112233445 is feed-confirmed MALICIOUS/dropper, created 41s before the alert and NOT quarantined [artifact:art_0001, ioc:sha256:b1946ac9...] -> it base64-decodes a blob into Invoke-Expression and runs Start-SyncLoop against metrics-telemetry-cdn.example:443 on a 15-second cycle [windows_events:evt_0193] -> DNS confirms the same PID resolved that domain to 203.0.113.66 [dns:dns_0001, dns:dns_0002] and flow telemetry shows four sessions to 203.0.113.66:443 at exact 15s intervals with uniform ~800B/~200B payloads [flows:flow_0101..0104] -> threat intel independently rates the domain MALICIOUS/c2 (first seen 2026-08-20) and IP SUSPICIOUS/c2-infrastructure [ioc:domain:metrics-telemetry-cdn.example, ioc:ip:203.0.113.66]. Persistence via HKCU Run value 'WinUpdateSync' [windows_events:evt_0196]. Risk 100/100 CRITICAL across 21 findings from 3 independent investigators; beacon_pattern corroborated by all three.

PROVEN vs LIKELY: PROVEN — execution, obfuscation, 15s beacon cadence to flagged infrastructure, persistence mechanism, TI matches. LIKELY — full dropper/second-stage behavior: the runtime-decoded body is the placeholder 'SYNTHETIC-DEMO-PAYLOAD', so post-decode actions were not statically observable (confidence 0.75 finding).

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY: (1) fallback C2 'update-sync-check.example' -> 198.51.100.23 was queried but never connected [dns:dns_0003]; feed-absent, link unconfirmed (conf 0.55). (2) explorer.exe running as CORP\jmalik spawning cmd.exe as CORP\svc_backup suggests possible credential theft/token manipulation of svc_backup [process_tree:proc_0049] — needs credential-response follow-up. (3) Minor timestamp inconsistency (script-block log 10:42:13Z vs file create 10:42:20Z) noted in evt_0195/evt_0193; execution anchored to process creation 10:42:11Z.
